title: Misleading
text:
Following your tax return, as indicated here, is misleading.  

First, the IRS encourages taxpayers to navigate the necessary jungle of online preparation and submission.

However, an insurmountable hurdle is the prerequisite of a cell phone number.  Even if you prepare all forms electronically and try to submit a completed tax return online, a functioning cell phone is required.  In 2021 my landline phone number was repeatedly rejected.  Whether a cell phone number is more secure, a better identifier, or whatever, no alternative mechanism exists to circumvent this requirement!

Subsequently, not having a home printer, I had to find a commercial business to print my iPad-prepared return, which was submitted via US Postal Service.

Second, the IRS2Go data apparently does not include returns sent by US Postal Service.  Tracking online the status of my 1040 return, submitted in early October 2021, has yielded no results as of early February 2022.

Luckily reaching an IRS agent by telephone, I confirmed that my tax return had been received.  However, no other information was available as to my anticipated refund.

Using IRS2Go, most recently as February 3, 2022, no online information is retrievable.  Having correctly entered all required data (Social Security number, date of birth, filing status, name, address, refund amount (as it appeared on my submitted return), IRS2Go repeatedly responded no match existed.  My entries were erroneous.  I should correct them and try again.

Thus, IRS statements on information about processing of returns and refunds are currently misleading, if not totally inaccurate.  

Even if problems of understaffing, inadequate funding, Covid-19, etc. exist, the IRS should amend its public claims.

Submitted on February 4, 2022.
